sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a trend [F168][F1][F10].
Revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion, then rose 153.2% in FY2021 and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [D161][F5][D200][F6][D238][F7].
The FY2022 increase came mainly from higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59].
Revenue then fell 20.5% in FY2023 on lower realized prices and has grown only 4.9% in FY2025, leaving the three-year CAGR at -5.3% [D274][P47][D342][D844].
Crude oil is the largest product line at 66.3% of FY2025 revenue, and it contributed just 0.1pp of the 4.9% growth that year [D551][D553][D342].
The U.S. supplied 79.1% of FY2025 revenue and 5.7pp of growth, while non-U.S. contributed 2.0pp [D382][D384][D400].
FY2025 sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, partly offset by lower realized crude and bitumen prices [P28].
Net income fell 13.6% while revenue rose 4.9%, and basic EPS fell 18.7% against that net income decline as the diluted share count rose 6.1% [D343][D342][D344][D356].
Cost of revenue grew 11.6% in FY2025 against revenue growth of 4.9%, so operating costs grew faster than revenue [D352][D342].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025, below the 17.9% window median and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [F30][D831][D830].
The FY2025 decline included higher DD&A of $1.3 billion and higher production and operating expenses of $875 million, primarily driven by the Marathon Oil acquisition [P17].
D&A rose to 19.5% of revenue in FY2025 from 17.5% in FY2024, and the effective tax rate rose to 36.9% from 32.4% [D330][D296][D332][D298].
Net margin fell 3.3pp in FY2025, and lower equity earnings of $370 million weighed on the below-the-line result [D351][P27].
Operating cash flow of $19.8 billion was 2.48x net income in FY2025, above the 2.18x of FY2024 [F59][D333][D299].
The decline in operating cash flow to $19.8 billion from $20.1 billion resulted from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by operations from the 2024 Marathon Oil acquisition [F59][F58][P6].
Free cash flow margin peaked at 24.1% in FY2021 against a 12.2% window median, and capex ran at 12.9% of revenue in FY2022 against D&A of 9.6% [D185][D834][D222][D221].
Stock-based compensation was only 1.7% of operating cash flow in FY2025, so conversion is not flattered by equity pay [D334].
Net cash was $7.1 billion, or 12.1% of revenue, in FY2025, against a -7.7% peer median and in the 100th percentile of six energy peers [D337][D338][D851][D850].
Cash and investments rose 13.4% to $8.1 billion while total debt fell 1.4% to $1.0 billion [D357][D335][D358][D336].

FY2025 uses included $12.6 billion of capital investment, $5.0 billion of buybacks, $4.0 billion of dividends and $0.9 billion of debt retirement, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sale proceeds [P7].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow, and the diluted share count still rose 6.1% [P31][D356].
The revenue series mixes presentations: FY2025 shows $51.8 billion in the table against $58.9 billion as first reported, and every year from FY2016 differs similarly [F10][X10][F1][X1].
Growth and margin comparisons that span a recast year and a first-reported year mix two bases, so the CAGR and margin history should be read with that caveat [F168][D831].
Revenue fell 20.5% in FY2023, the one clear down year outside FY2020, on lower realized commodity prices [D274][P47].
A single price-driven decline in a cyclical producer is not by itself a structural warning, but it shows how quickly the top line reverses.
Segment revenue members sum to 227% of consolidated revenue in FY2025 because some are totals of others [R4].
Segment shares cannot be added across members, so concentration should be read from the largest single line rather than a sum [D551].
Whether net margin holds above the 17.9% window median or slips further from the 15.4% FY2025 level, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D831][F30].
Whether operating cash flow stays above the $19.8 billion FY2025 level as lower commodity prices persist, per the FY2026 cash flow statement [F59][P6].
Whether net cash as a share of revenue stays above the 12.1% FY2025 level after the $5 billion disposition target is completed by year-end 2026 [D338][P32].
